value: The International System of Units (SI) defines seven base units—the second (time), metre (length), kilogram (mass), ampere (electric current), kelvin (thermodynamic temperature), mole (amount of substance), and candela (luminous intensity)—which form the fundamental basis for all other derived units in modern science and technology. Historically defined through various means, including physical artifacts, a significant revision effective May 2019 redefined all base units by linking them to fixed numerical values of fundamental physical constants, such as the Planck constant and elementary charge. This redefinition enhances the universality, precision, and long-term stability of the SI system, moving away from reliance on changeable or replicable physical objects.
